title: Integral-closure coproduct comparison for normalization at a stalk
statement: Let a:P -> N be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], s a point of N, and R = O_(N,s) [def-weil-residue-field]. Let n be a natural number and E_i (i in Fin n) fields [def-weil-field] equipped with R-algebra structures. Suppose e identifies P times_N Spec R with the coproduct of Spec E_i [def-pc-fibre-product] over Spec R: e.hom followed by the coproduct of Spec(algebraMap R E_i) is the second pullback projection. Then there is an isomorphism from the pullback of the relative normalization of a [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] to the coproduct of Spec(integralClosure R E_i) [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], whose composition with the coproduct of their canonical R-structure maps is the second normalization pullback projection. No Cartier, DVR, group, finite extension, or module-finiteness hypothesis is required. The empty finite coproduct is included.

proof.text: Apply normalization stalk base change to identify the original normalization pulled back to Spec R with the relative normalization of the pulled-back source. The existing theorem is phrased using pullback of an arbitrary base morphism; use the identity base morphism and the canonical identity-pullback isomorphisms.

The supplied source isomorphism makes the pulled-back source affine, with R-algebra of sections the finite product of E_i. On the affine base Spec R, use normalizationObjIso to identify the normalization sections with the integral closure in these source sections. Integral closure in a finite product is coordinatewise: projection preserves integrality; conversely the product of the finitely many monic annihilating polynomials annihilates the tuple. This gives an R-algebra equivalence with the product of integralClosure R E_i.

Apply Spec to the algebra equivalence and the finite product/coproduct isomorphism sigmaSpec, reindexing via ULift if needed. All comparison maps commute with R-algebra maps. The given source structure equation and fromNormalization_app therefore prove the displayed structural-map equation. When n=0 the product is the zero ring and both spectra are empty.

lean.statement:
theorem normalization_stalk_field_coproduct
    {N P : Scheme.{u}} (a : P ⟶ N) [QuasiCompact a] [QuasiSeparated a]
    (s : N) (n : ℕ) (E : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (E i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra (N.presheaf.stalk s) (E i)]
    (e : pullback a (N.fromSpecStalk s) ≅
      ∐ fun i : Fin n ↦ Spec (CommRingCat.of (E i)))
    (he : e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i : Fin n ↦ Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (N.presheaf.stalk s) (E i)))) =
        pullback.snd a (N.fromSpecStalk s)) :
    ∃ e' : pullback a.fromNormalization (N.fromSpecStalk s) ≅
        ∐ fun i : Fin n ↦
          Spec (CommRingCat.of (integralClosure (N.presheaf.stalk s) (E i))),
      e'.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i : Fin n ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap (N.presheaf.stalk s) (integralClosure (N.presheaf.stalk s) (E i))))) =
          pullback.snd a.fromNormalization (N.fromSpecStalk s)
